explanation: Green's Problem 45 (Erdős): for all large N, can one choose a residue a_p for every prime p ≤ N so that every m ∈ [1, N] lies in at least 10 of the classes? The encoding counts the primes p ≤ N with a_p ≡ m (mod p). Using ∀ᶠ N matches Erdős' formulation (erdosproblems.com/689: "Let n be sufficiently large…"). The statement is faithful.
